name: Ziba
bio: Ziba was a servant of Saul's household whom David summoned to ask if anyone of Saul's line remained, so that he might show them kindness for Jonathan's sake. Ziba told David of Jonathan's crippled son Mephibosheth, living in Lo-debar in the house of Machir son of Ammiel (2 Samuel 9:1-4). After David restored to Mephibosheth all the land that had belonged to Saul, he put Ziba — who had fifteen sons and twenty servants of his own — in charge of farming that land on Mephibosheth's behalf, so that Mephibosheth could eat at the king's table (2 Samuel 9:9-12). When David fled Jerusalem during Absalom's rebellion, Ziba met him just past the top of the hill with donkeys loaded with bread, raisins, summer fruit, and wine for David's weary household. When David asked where Mephibosheth was, Ziba claimed he had stayed behind in Jerusalem, hoping that "today the Israelites will restore to me my grandfather's kingdom" — a claim David took at face value, granting Ziba everything that had belonged to Mephibosheth on the spot (2 Samuel 16:1-4). Whether Ziba's account was true becomes a contested question when David returns to Jerusalem, a story told in detail in the chapters ahead.
